title: VIP Escalation Intake: Elastic Runway & Commitment Swap Simulator
creator: Aisha Carter
description: Create a customer-driven intake and prioritization workflow for VIP escalations that supports elastic delivery runways, feature-swap commitments between accounts, and a simulator to quantify tradeoffs and release risk. This will enable Sales/CS and PMs to negotiate commitments with customers transparently while preserving roadmap predictability.
background: Top accounts have increased requests for guaranteed delivery windows and partial commitments. Current intake is ad-hoc: Slack threads and one-off promises have caused scope creep and missed expectations. Need a formalized policy and tooling that allows temporary resource reservation, conditional swaps, and measurable impact on backlog and OKRs.
proposed_solution: 1) Intake form extension capturing delivery window flexibility, must-have vs nice-to-have, and willingness to accept swaps or credits. 2) Elastic Runway policy: define soft vs hard commitments with time-boxed hold on capacity. 3) Commitment Swap primitive: allow two accounts to exchange prioritized slots under guardrails (credits, scope reduction, delivery window). 4) Simulator UI in Console: project the impact of accepting a VIP ask on OKRs, sprint capacity, release dates, and churn risk. 5) Operational playbook: negotiation templates, SLA text, and post-commit monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Intake schema added to Console form and accessible to CS via link
Policy definitions for soft/hard commitments documented and approved by Legal and Sales
Simulator MVP shows projected release date shift and OKR slippage for a given acceptance scenario
Commitment Swap workflow exists with audit trail and CS/Legal sign-off step
Two pilot VIP escalations processed end-to-end using the new flow with retrospective notes
metrics: Number of ad-hoc commitments reduced by 80% in pilot accounts
Accuracy of simulator projection within +/- 10% of observed release shift after pilot
CS satisfaction score for negotiation process >= 4/5
Number of swaps executed and credits issued tracked
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Define intake schema and Elastic Runway policy, legal template drafts
Phase 2 (4 weeks): Build Console form changes and simulator backend model (capacity/OKR model)
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Internal trial with Sales/CS on 3 accounts and iterate
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Pilot with 2 strategic customers under contract addendum
Phase 5: Post-pilot review and wider rollout, documentation and training
stakeholders: Sales/CS: Maya Singh (Lead AE), Jordan Park (CSM)
risks: Simulator model underestimates integration work leading to overcommitment
Sales pushes for hard commitments without proper credits or SLA compensation
Complexity of swap agreements increases legal overhead
Pilot accounts may decline to participate resulting in limited validation data
open_questions: What guardrails should distinguish soft vs hard commitments?
How many sprint cycles can be reserved without impacting roadmap predictability?
What credit currency (time/feature/discount) should be standard for swaps?
Does commitment swap require signed amendment or is digital acceptance sufficient?
